detail:
The international multidisciplinary consensus on POTS and dysautonomia describes care that starts with recognizing orthostatic intolerance and educating the person about their form of dysautonomia. Non-drug measures come first for many people: expanding fluid and salt intake when a clinician judges it appropriate, compression garments that limit blood pooling in the legs and abdomen, physical counterpressure maneuvers, and a structured exercise program that usually begins with recumbent or semi-recumbent activity.

When medications are used, the consensus describes them as matched to the dominant problem, for example heart-rate control, blood-vessel constriction, or blood-volume support, rather than one drug for dysautonomia itself. Frequently overlapping conditions, such as migraine, mast cell activation, and gastrointestinal dysmotility, are addressed as part of the same plan.

Talk to your doctor before starting or changing any medication.

Tabs is not endorsing or verifying this material.
sourceVideoTitle: Postural orthostatic tachycardia syndrome (POTS) and dysautonomia: International multidisciplinary expert consensus
summary: An international expert consensus in The American Journal of Medicine describes dysautonomia management built on education, non-drug measures, and medications matched to the person's dominant symptoms, because no single treatment fits every form.
takeaways: education and trigger awareness are the foundation sources describe
fluids, salt, and compression help some forms; targets are individual
exercise is usually recumbent or semi-recumbent at first
medicines target specific symptoms; never start or change them without your doctor
title: Managing dysautonomia day to day
